title: Chemical Equilibrium

notes.heading: 1. Law of Mass Action, Kp vs Kc & Equilibrium Constant Algebra
notes.proseLatex: For $aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD$, pure solids and pure liquids have unit activity and are OMITTED from $K_c$ and $K_p$ (e.g., $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$ has $K_p = p_{\text{CO}_2}$!). Ideal gases satisfy $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$ where $\Delta n_g = (c+d) - (a+b)$ counts ONLY gaseous moles. Reversing a reaction inverts $K' = 1/K$, multiplying stoichiometry by $m$ raises $K' = K^m$, and adding two equilibria multiplies $K_{\text{net}} = K_1 K_2$.

keyFormulas.label: Kp–Kc Relation & Stoichiometric Scaling Rules
keyFormulas.latex: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g},\qquad \text{reverse}: K' = \frac{1}{K},\qquad \times m: K' = K^m$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Relate Kp and Kc (watch gaseous moles only!) and combine multi-step equilibrium constants.

notes.heading: 2. Reaction Quotient Qc, Le Chatelier's Principle & Inert-Gas Addition
notes.proseLatex: Comparing $Q_c$ to $K_c$: $Q_c < K_c$ drives forward reaction, $Q_c > K_c$ drives reverse. Increasing total pressure (decreasing volume) shifts equilibrium toward FEWER gas moles ($\Delta n_g$ side). Raising temperature shifts toward the ENDOTHERMIC direction (and is the ONLY disturbance that changes the numerical value of $K$, via van 't Hoff $\ln\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{\Delta H^\circ}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)$). Adding inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME changes no partial pressures so equilibrium does NOT shift; at CONSTANT PRESSURE it increases volume and shifts toward MORE gas moles!

keyFormulas.label: van 't Hoff Temperature Dependence of K
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Predict temperature, pressure, catalyst, and inert-gas effects on equilibrium.

notes.heading: 3. Haber (NH₃) & Contact (SO₃) Industrial Equilibria
notes.proseLatex: Both Haber's ammonia synthesis ($\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3,\; \Delta H < 0,\; \Delta n_g = -2$) and Contact $\text{SO}_3$ oxidation ($2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3,\; \Delta H < 0,\; \Delta n_g = -1$) are exothermic mole-decreasing reactions: high pressure favours yield thermodynamically, while an optimum moderate temperature ($\sim 700\text{ K}$) plus catalyst ($\text{Fe}$ with $\text{Mo}/\text{K}_2\text{O}$ promoter in Haber; $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ in Contact) balances kinetic rate without destroying $K$.

keyFormulas.label: Haber & Contact Process Conditions
keyFormulas.latex: $\text{Haber: Fe catalyst, }200\text{ atm, }\sim 700\text{ K};\qquad \text{Contact: V}_2\text{O}_5\text{ catalyst, }1\text{--}2\text{ atm, }\sim 720\text{ K}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Recall industrial catalysts and why moderate T rather than 0 C is used.

wbjeebTraps: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse rates EQUALLY — it cuts time to reach equilibrium but NEVER changes $K_c$, $K_p$, or equilibrium yield!
Adding inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME produces ZERO shift for every reaction; only CONSTANT-PRESSURE inert-gas addition shifts toward higher gas moles (when $\Delta n_g \neq 0$).
Count ONLY gaseous species in $\Delta n_g$: for $\text{C}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}(g)$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1$ (ignore solid carbon!).

conceptPrimer.heading: Law of Mass Action & the Activity Rule
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: For $aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD$, $K_c = \frac{[C]^c[D]^d}{[A]^a[B]^b}$ with PURE solids and liquids OMITTED (unit activity): $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$ gives $K_p = p_{\text{CO}_2}$ alone. Micro-check: drop anything with a fixed activity from the expression.

conceptPrimer.heading: $K_p$ vs $K_c$: the $\Delta n_g$ Bridge
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$ where $\Delta n_g$ counts ONLY gaseous moles, products minus reactants: for $\text{C}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}(g)$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1$ (ignore solid carbon). $\Delta n_g = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$. Micro-check: $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$: $\Delta n_g = -2$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Equilibrium-Algebra Rules
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Reverse the reaction $\Rightarrow K' = 1/K$; multiply stoichiometry by $m$ $\Rightarrow K' = K^m$; add two equilibria $\Rightarrow K_{\text{net}} = K_1K_2$. These three moves solve most JELET manipulation questions. Micro-check: halving a reaction takes $K^{1/2}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Reaction Quotient $Q$ and Le Chatelier
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $Q$ uses the same expression as $K$ but at non-equilibrium concentrations: $Q < K$ drives forward, $Q > K$ reverse. Pressure up (volume down) shifts toward FEWER gas moles; temperature up shifts toward the ENDOTHERMIC side — the only disturbance that changes the numerical $K$ (van 't Hoff: $\ln\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{\Delta H^\circ}{R}(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2})$). Micro-check: a catalyst never shifts $Q$ or $K$ — it only shortens the ride.

conceptPrimer.heading: Inert Gas: Two Very Different Outcomes
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Adding inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME changes no partial pressures $\Rightarrow$ zero shift, every time. At CONSTANT PRESSURE the volume grows, every partial pressure dilutes equally $\Rightarrow$ shift toward MORE gas moles. Micro-check: inert + fixed $V$ is the standard trick answer.

conceptPrimer.heading: Haber & Contact: Industry Applies Le Chatelier
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Both $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$ ($\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta n_g = -2$) and $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$ ($\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta n_g = -1$) are exothermic and mole-decreasing: high pressure favours yield, moderate $\sim 700\,\text{K}$ balances rate against $K$, catalysts ($\text{Fe}$ with promoter; $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$) speed both directions equally. Micro-check: catalysts change time-to-equilibrium, never yield.

memoryHooks: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$; gases only in $\Delta n_g$.
Reverse: invert. Scale: exponentiate. Add: multiply.
Pressure up: run to the fewer-moles side.
Inert at fixed $P$: run to more moles.
Haber and Contact both hate heat and love pressure.
commonMistakes: Leaving solids or liquids inside $K$ expressions.
Believing a catalyst shifts the position of equilibrium.
Adding inert gas at fixed volume and expecting a shift.
Forgetting that only temperature changes the numerical $K$.
Applying the wrong exponent when scaling stoichiometry.
Predicting higher yield at higher temperature for exothermic processes.
examChecklist: Strip solids and liquids before writing $K$.
Count only gaseous moles in $\Delta n_g$.
Use invert, exponentiate, multiply for $K$ algebra.
Apply van 't Hoff for temperature jumps.
Know Haber and Contact catalysts and $\Delta n_g$.
